question: Which Cluster I estero labels in the DENR-NCR 2025 Pasig River system management list have independent official or environmental-document name support, and which name forms or scope counts remain unresolved?
method: Compared the fifteen Cluster I labels from the linked DENR-NCR Annual Report 2025 scope review against the EMB-DMS-hosted Manila North WRF EPRMP drainage-map appendix, the EMB-hosted 2020 LRT Line 2 West Extension EIS, and a 2019 DENR announcement of the Manila estero cleanup partnership. Exact name strings, name-form candidates, inventory counts, and map descriptions were kept separate. No waterway geometry, canonical feature match, fish evidence, or app record was inferred.

clusterScope.retrieval: Used the Cluster I fifteen-name list and Manila City cluster context already reviewed from the official PDF text extraction in the linked scope artifact. Direct PDF access was unavailable in this pass; no access restriction was bypassed and no PDF or list image was retained.

independentSources.retrieval: Official EMB Integrated Information System Document Management System PDF opened. Reviewed the reproduced MMDA Drainage Map of Manila City, Figure 2.2-2, printed p. 2.2-3, including the listed North Manila and Central Manila waterways. No map image, table, or geometry retained.

Official EMB EIA-hosted July 2020 EIS opened. Reviewed section 2.3, “Waterways and Esteros,” Table 2-12 and Figure 2-38, printed p. 2-59. The EIS attributes the list to Manila CLUP 2005–2020. No EIS map or table copied.

Reviewed the DENR-NCR article through official DENR search-index text and an official DENR regional mirror that states the partnership and named esteros; the NCR article fetch returned HTTP 403. The article is a 2019 cleanup partnership list, not a current inventory or waterway survey.

inventoryCountConflict.eisSummary: The 2020 LRT Line 2 EIS text describes 29 esteros in Manila (19 North and 10 South) and 31.812 km total length, alongside one creek and two open canals.
inventoryCountConflict.eisNamedTable: The named “List of Existing Estero” reproduced in Figure 2-38 enumerates 20 esteros, of which 13 match Cluster I names; other listed entries belong to different Manila lists/clusters.
inventoryCountConflict.disposition: The summary count and visible named list do not reconcile in the reviewed text. Treat the EIS as corroboration for listed names only, not a complete or current Manila waterway inventory.

rightsDecision.decision: Keep short attributed name/locality findings as internal research notes. The EIS states that its list derives from the Manila CLUP and the EPRMP reproduces an MMDA drainage map; neither hosting nor derivation grants a blanket right to republish source maps, tables, or geometry.

limitations: The 2025 DENR-NCR report is a management list, not a complete, independently surveyed inventory of Manila esteros.
The LRT EIS states a total of 29 esteros in Manila but the reviewed named table enumerates 20; this discrepancy remains unresolved and means the EIS list is not treated as complete.
The EPRMP and LRT EIS reproduce/attribute municipal planning and MMDA map material; no map or geometry is republished from them.
Name support and city/district context do not establish a unique channel, route, boundary, water quality, current condition, fish presence, public access, fishing permission, or safety.
The Uli-uli source forms differ; no alias or feature match is confirmed.
No fish, species, occurrence, access, legal, hazard, geometry, or public-app claims are admitted.
